ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, within circle $\odot O$, the diameter $AB$ intersects with the chord $CD$ at point $P$, $\angle CAB=40^\circ$, $\angle APD=65^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle DAB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $\because \angle APD = \angle C + \angle CAB$,\\
$\therefore \angle C = \angle APD - \angle CAB = 65^\circ - 40^\circ = 25^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle B = \angle C = 25^\circ$.\\
Because $AB$ is the diameter of $\odot O$, $\therefore \angle ADB = 90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle DAB = 90^\circ - \angle B = 90^\circ - 25^\circ = \boxed{65^\circ}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, within circle $\odot O$, the diameter $AB$ intersects the chord $CD$ at point $P$, $\angle CAB = 40^\circ$, and $\angle APD = 65^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle DAB$?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Given $\angle APD = \angle C + \angle CAB$, $\angle C = 65^\circ - 40^\circ = 25^\circ$. Therefore $\angle B = \angle C = 25^\circ$. Since $AB$ is the diameter of $\odot O$, $\angle ADB = 90^\circ$. Hence $\angle DAB = 90^\circ - 25^\circ = 65^\circ$.
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure there is a circle, A is on the left side of the circumference, B is on the right side of the circumference, and AB is a diameter passing through the center O of the circle; chord CD connects from C above to D at the lower left, and intersects AB at point P. P is located at the intersection of AB and CD, C is above AB, and D is below AB and to the left. The problem gives ∠CAB = 40°, ∠APD = 65°.

Then reason: Because P is on AB, ray AP is collinear with AB, so ∠CAP = ∠CAB = 40°. In triangle APC, P, C, D are collinear, and ray PD is the opposite extension of ray PC, so ∠APD is the exterior angle of triangle APC at point P. By the exterior angle theorem, ∠APD = ∠CAP + ∠ACP. Substituting gives 65° = 40° + ∠ACP, so ∠ACP = 25°. Also because P is on CD, ∠ACP = ∠ACD = 25°. In the circle, ∠ACD and ∠ABD are both inscribed angles subtending the same chord AD, therefore ∠ABD = 25°. Since AB is a diameter, according to the fact that the inscribed angle subtending a diameter is a right angle, ∠ADB = 90°. In triangle ABD, ∠DAB = 180° - 90° - 25° = 65°.
